decision: Not adopted: an exception to 'commit the floor churn make test leaves' for a dependency floor that bmk lowered or moved back across a major version.
reopen_if: A bmk run lowers a dependency floor again, or bmk's CHANGELOG reverts the 3.22.7 behaviour.
why: Fixed in bmk itself: since 3.22.7 bmk no longer lowers a dependency floor when no single release installs on every supported Python, so the churn the skill says to commit no longer holds a lowered floor.

decision: Not adopted: advice that bmk's floor update can pick a release PyPI is still uploading, so a red gate should be re-run after restoring pyproject.toml and uv.lock.
reopen_if: bmk drops or shortens its cooldown, or a gate fails resolving a third-party release younger than the cooldown.
why: Measured on bmk 3.33.1: bmk writes its 7-day cooldown into the project before locking and judges a third-party floor only against releases uploaded before that cutoff, so a release minutes old cannot be chosen. Index lag on the project's own freshly published package is already covered in the skill.

decision: Not adopted: having bmk pin every declared floor younger than the cooldown, existing floors included, before its first lock attempt.
reopen_if: A bmk deps update leaves a declared floor younger than the cooldown unpinned, with that run's full update_deps output kept.
why: Did not reproduce on bmk 3.33.2: replaying the reported pyproject.toml against PyPI as of the reported cutoff wrote the young floor's exclude-newer pin along with the others, and a real bmk deps update on a copy pinned and passed. Other projects with the same young floor got the same pin at the time. The failing run's log was gone; the likeliest cause is a transient PyPI answer whose one-line notice a filtered view of the output hid.

anchors: WITHOUT the rewrites the gate just made
decision: A gate run after the commit it gates (make test && git push, or a gate jig with a follow-up push) pushes that commit without the gate's own rewrites: read git status --porcelain after every gate run and commit what bmk changed. A separate chore commit is as good as amending, and the only form after the push.

evidence.text: ruff 0.17.4 from bmk 3.33.3's tool env reformatted a fenced python block in a scratch .md with plain ruff format, and bmk's format stage runs ruff format over the whole tree. A RED probe on the pre-edit text answered NONE for Markdown and for amend-versus-separate; GREEN probes (opus, haiku) quoted the new sentences.

reopen_if: bmk's test stages stop rewriting the tree, or ruff format stops reformatting fenced Python blocks in Markdown files.
why: The skill said to commit bmk's churn with the change and covered make push, which commits after its gate. It was silent on a gate run over an already-made commit, where the floor raises, the relocked uv.lock and ruff's rewrites (fenced Python blocks in Markdown included) stay behind as uncommitted edits while the push reports success.

anchors: `UV_PYTHON` does not choose the interpreter a gate runs on.** bmk
decision: UV_PYTHON does not choose the interpreter a bmk gate runs on: with a Python minor classifier declared, bmk passes the highest declared minor to uv as an explicit --python and rebuilds a .venv on another minor. Another minor is gated with make test-all or CI, and a report of a local gate names the interpreter it ran on. With no classifier declared, the variable decides only when bmk creates a missing .venv.

evidence.text: bmk 3.33.3 source: no occurrence of UV_PYTHON; desired_python_minor returns the last of all_python_minors; _create_venv and _sync_from_lock pass --python <minor>; discard_venv_on_wrong_python removes a venv whose version differs from uv's target. uv 0.13.0: UV_PYTHON=3.14 uv venv --python 3.15 built 3.15.0, without --python it built 3.14.8. Field report 2026-11-17: project .venv dirs on 3.15.0 after gates run with UV_PYTHON=3.14.

reopen_if: bmk starts reading UV_PYTHON, or stops passing --python to uv venv and uv sync (adapters/stagerunner/venv.py: desired_python_minor, _create_venv, _sync_from_lock).
why: A reader who sets UV_PYTHON=3.14 before make test in a project declaring 3.14 and 3.15 gets a 3.15 gate and reports it as a 3.14 result; nothing in the output says otherwise.

anchors: A raised runtime floor needs a CHANGELOG line, and bmk writes none.
decision: Before a bump, compare [project].dependencies with the last tag and, when a requirement moved, add one 'runtime dependency floors raised: ...' line under [Unreleased]; bmk writes no CHANGELOG line for a floor it raises.

evidence.text: bmk 3.33.3 source: CHANGELOG.md is written only by the bump helper (_bump_version.update_changelog, heading rename). The shipped command, run in the bmk checkout: no output against the last tag v3.33.3 (rc 0), 20 lines (10 changed requirements, a - and a + line each) against v3.30.0.

reopen_if: bmk writes a CHANGELOG entry for a floor it raises, or stops raising floors in [project].dependencies.
why: The floor update raises runtime requirements along with dev ones and the bump only renames the CHANGELOG heading, so a release can ship changed install requirements with no changelog line.
